# pluma

An open-source bounded-context and export engine for CSV, XLSX, and Parquet, plus a
Markdown-to-PDF document engine without Chromium or LaTeX. Node library + CLI + MCP.
Install: `npm install @ararahq/pluma`.

## Dataset context

```ts
import { compileContext, openContext } from "@ararahq/pluma"
const job = compileContext("ledger.parquet", { output: "ledger.pluma" })
await job.result()
const context = openContext("ledger.pluma")
const result = context.query({
  filter: [{ column: "status", op: "eq", value: "paid" }],
  groupBy: ["country"],
  metrics: [{ column: "amount", aggregate: "sum", as: "revenue" }],
})
const payload = result.payload({ tokenBudget: 4000, tokenizer: { id: "o200k_base", version: "1" } })
```

Use `context.inspect(...)` before querying, `context.sample(...)` for a deterministic head
sample, and `context.export({ format: "csv"|"xlsx"|"parquet", output })` for a streamed
artifact. Query results carry package fingerprint, plan hash, input block hashes, and exact
row counts. A `.pluma` package is an open directory containing a manifest, bounded Arrow IPC
blocks, Markdown overview/schema views, and source provenance.

CLI: `pluma context compile`, `inspect`, `query`, and `export`. MCP adds compile, durable
compile job inspect/cancel, inspect, sample, exact query, export, pin, and release tools.

## Generate a document (what an LLM should output)

Produce plain GFM Markdown with optional YAML frontmatter. Do NOT wrap the document in a
```markdown fence (pluma tolerates it, but plain is better).

```
---
title: Proposta comercial
subtitle: Escopo e investimento
author: Ana Silva
date: Agosto de 2026
brand: ./brand.json
---

## Section

Body text with **bold**, _italic_, `code`, [links](https://x.com), images, GFM tables,
nested lists, > blockquotes. `---` becomes a horizontal rule.
```

Supported: headings 1-6, paragraphs, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline+fenced code (with
syntax highlight), links, images (paths relative to the .md), blockquotes, ordered/unordered
nested lists, GFM tables with `:--`/`--:` alignment, horizontal rules. Raw HTML is dropped.
All text is escaped — Markdown cannot inject Typst code.

## In-document controls

- `<!-- pagebreak -->` — force a page break.
- `<!-- columns:2 -->` ... `<!-- /columns -->` — 2-4 balanced text columns (content between
  the markers stays normal Markdown).
- ```` ```typst ```` fenced block — raw Typst island for free-form layout (mixed font sizes,
  colored boxes, grids). Full Typst language available inside. Trusted-author feature.

Example island:

```typst
#text(size: 18pt, weight: 700)[Big] #text(size: 8pt, style: "italic")[small italic]
#block(fill: rgb("#ecfeff"), radius: 6pt, inset: 12pt)[Callout box]
```

## Brand (visual identity) — brand.json

All keys optional. Colors are hex. Lengths use pt/mm/cm/in/em.

```json
{
  "fonts": { "body": "Geist", "heading": "Geist", "mono": "Geist Mono", "size": 10.5 },
  "colors": { "text": "#18181b", "muted": "#71717a", "faint": "#a1a1aa",
              "accent": "#0e7490", "link": "#0e7490", "border": "#d4d4d8",
              "codeBackground": "#f4f4f5" },
  "page": { "paper": "a4", "marginX": "2.2cm", "marginY": "2.4cm" },
  "logo": { "path": "assets/logo.png", "width": "3.2cm" },
  "footer": "Company — site.com"
}
```

Discovery: a `brand.json` next to the .md is used automatically; `brand:` in frontmatter
points elsewhere; `--brand` flag overrides both. A `fonts/` dir next to the .md (or the
brand.json) is picked up automatically for .ttf/.otf files.

## CLI

```
pluma doc.md                  # zero config; auto-discovers brand.json and fonts/
pluma doc.md -o out.pdf       # explicit output
pluma doc.md --json           # one JSON line: {"ok":true,"output":"...","bytes":...}
pluma doc.pdf --json          # {"ok":true,"markdown":"...","meta":...,"warnings":...}
pluma doc.md --typst --json   # {"ok":true,"typst":"..."}
                              # failures: {"ok":false,"error":{"message":"..."}}
pluma doc.md --typst          # emit generated Typst source instead of compiling
pluma doc.md -w               # watch mode, recompiles on save
pluma doc.pdf                 # PDF -> doc.md
pluma page.html -o page.md    # HTML -> Markdown
pluma https://example.com     # URL -> Markdown on stdout
pluma mcp                     # MCP server over stdio, safe mode
pluma mcp --trusted-local     # raw Typst/filesystem access; trusted agents only
```

## Node API

```ts
import { renderPdf } from "@ararahq/pluma"
const pdf: Uint8Array = renderPdf(markdown, {
  brand: { fonts: { body: "Geist" }, footer: "Co" },  // same shape as brand.json
  fontPaths: ["./fonts"],   // dirs with .ttf/.otf
  root: "./docs",           // base dir for logo/image paths
})
```

Also exported: `markdownToTypstSource(md, opts)` (debug the generated Typst),
`createTheme(brand)`, `normalizeInput(md)` (strips a wrapping ```markdown fence),
errors `UnknownThemeError`, `InvalidBrandError` (invalid hex/length values).

For hosted/multi-tenant rendering, use `renderPdfCloudSafe(markdown, { brand?, meta? })`.
It rejects raw Typst, Markdown images, and filesystem-backed/unknown brand fields, then returns
`{ pdf: Uint8Array, pageCount: number }`. The unrestricted local `renderPdf` API is unchanged.

## Read API

```ts
import { readPdf, readPdfPages, countPdfPages, readHtml, readUrl } from "@ararahq/pluma"

const pdf = readPdf("./doc.pdf")
pdf.markdown
pdf.pages
pdf.meta.pageCount
pdf.warnings

const html = readHtml(source, { baseUrl: "https://example.com/post" })
const remote = await readUrl("https://example.com/post", { maxTokens: 4000 })
```

`readPdf` accepts a path, Buffer, or Uint8Array. Options: `pages` (for example `"1-3,7"`),
`pageBreaks` (`none|rule|marker`), `headings`, `tables`, `dropHeadersFooters`, `maxPages`,
`maxBytes`, and `onWarning`. `readPdfPages` iterates decoded pages asynchronously without
retaining prior page content. `countPdfPages` walks the page tree without decoding content.
PDF reading uses the existing text layer; OCR and non-empty passwords are not supported.

`readHtml`/`readUrl` options: `mode` (`article|page|raw`), `images`, `links`, `frontMatter`,
`maxTokens`, `keepSelectors`, and `dropSelectors`. `readUrl` also supports `timeoutMs`,
`maxBytes`, `maxRedirects`, `headers`, `userAgent`, and `networkPolicy`. Network access is
public-only and DNS-pinned by default; use `networkPolicy: "any"` only for trusted intranet URLs.
`readUrl` does not execute JavaScript. A client-rendered SPA may therefore expose only its
initial loading shell and metadata; use a browser-capable upstream and pass its HTML to
`readHtml` when JavaScript rendering is required.

## MCP tools (pluma mcp)

Tool `render_pdf`, arguments: `markdown` (string, required), `output_path` (a `.pdf`
inside the current working directory), and a cloud-safe `brand` object. Safe mode rejects
raw Typst, images, custom font paths, filesystem roots, traversal, and symlink escapes.
`fonts_dir` and `root` are exposed only with `--trusted-local`. Register: command `pluma`,
args `["mcp"]`.

Tool `read_pdf`: `pdf_path` (absolute path, required), `pages`, `page_breaks`,
`drop_headers_footers`. Tool `read_html`: `html` (required), `base_url`, `mode`, `images`,
`links`, `front_matter`, `max_tokens`. Tool `read_url`: `url` (required), the HTML options,
plus `timeout_ms` and `max_bytes`.

All successful CLI operations with `--json` preserve their operation-specific
fields inside a top-level `{ "ok": true, ... }` envelope and emit one JSON line
per completion. This includes render, PDF/HTML/URL read, Typst-source, and help
results; watch mode emits one envelope per rebuild.
